analysis:
The only changed file is the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift. The patch adds a ReclaimableMemory test helper (new lines ~96-118) and a test, shortSampleReclaimsBeforeSkipping (~196-218), covering StartupPreloader's new reclaimBeforeSkip and currentRequiredGb hooks. The supplied units are base text only. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the head side of the test and the production StartupPreloader changes are not visible.

No production code, network surface, key handling, attestation, or authorization paths are changed in the supplied evidence. The test uses scripted closures, no real model weights, a temp-directory persistence file, and a stub coordinator, and does not touch the SSD prefix cache at rest (T-041), the X25519 key (A-003), or the coordinator websocket contract (TB-002). The tests write only to temp directories. One test writes a fake HF snapshot into the real HF cache directory for the duration of the test and removes it in a defer, which is test hygiene and not a security regression.

The reclaimBeforeSkip hook in the production preloader may release retained KV segments or the buffer pool before a memory-admission skip. This could interact with T-028 (residual GPU memory) and T-041 (retained prefix cache), but the production implementation is outside the supplied evidence. A later pass should confirm that the reclaim does not weaken the no-eviction admission guarantee or bypass the KV grant floors, and that it does not purge or alter cache scope/TTL semantics. No finding is raised because there is no visible evidence of a regression.
